result_text:
I fixed the four broken default conventions in `ScopingConventions.java`, and added a regression test. The full `codeanalyzer` suite passes offline (337 run, 0 failures, 3 skipped, all pre-existing).

**Changes in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`:**
- **pkgdown / Doxygen / meta-generator rules** (around line 327): the path pattern `(html|html|xhtml)` is now `(htm|html|xhtml)`, so `.htm` pages are covered.
- **.NET `<doc>` XML rule** (around line 295): `.*/[.]xml` is now `.*[.]xml`, so `MyAssembly.xml` matches.
- **JavaScript `// Generated by` rule** (around line 294): `.*/[.]js` is now `.*[.]js`, so `app.js` matches.
- **Gradle JavaScript rule** (line 224, build-and-deployment): `.*[.][-]gradle[.]js` is now `.*[-]gradle[.]js`, so `build-gradle.js` matches.

**New test:** `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsDefaultsTest.java` has 7 cases. They cover the positive cases (`.htm` pkgdown/Doxygen/meta pages, `.html` Doxygen, `.xhtml` meta page, `<doc>` XML, `// Generated by` JS, `build-gradle.js`, `build.gradle`) and the negative cases (hand-written `.htm`, `.html`, `.xml`, `.js`, and `src/app.js` in build scope). All 7 pass.

I did not confirm that the new test fails on the original code. I tried a stash-based check, but it would have touched your working tree, so I skipped it. The fix is still verified by the passing tests on the new code. Nothing is committed.
